accuracy.evidence: Command word meanings follow AQA command words pages (GCSE Science, built on the Ofqual list): describe means recall facts, events or a process accurately; explain means state the reasons; compare means set out similarities or differences, not just write about one thing; evaluate means weigh evidence for and against to reach a judgement. The challenge timing (90 minutes for 80 marks, so about 7 minutes for 6 marks) matches AQA GCSE Maths papers of 1 hour 30 minutes and 80 marks. The minute-a-mark rule is always worked out from the paper, never stated as a fixed law.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the mistakes named in the adult text: answering the topic and not the command word, writing about one thing when asked to compare, believing more detail earns explain marks without reasons, ending an evaluate answer with no judgement, giving every question equal time, and sinking far too long into a stuck low-mark question. Each has its own feedback line in the lab and the challenge.

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanics are specific to exam technique: matching four answers on one topic to the command word each obeys, adding reason chips to a describe answer while a marks meter and word count show that detail with no reason scores nothing, dragging six time bars against a 45-minute budget, a for/against balance with an off-topic point to leave out, and marking three scripts against a mark scheme. The distinctness gate passed against all other flag labs, including Teaching It Back and Using and Evaluating Textual Evidence.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners find each rule by doing: a wrong match names the command word the answer actually obeys, a detail chip adds words but not marks, an even 7.5 minute split leaves Q1 overfunded and Q6 short until the bars follow the marks, the colours point bounces as off-topic, and a script marked wrongly cites the mark scheme line it misses. Each finished step states the rule in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: that a long, detailed description scores well on an evaluate question, that more detail about the graph earns explain marks, and that each question should get the same time (about 7 minutes). The matching, the marks meter and the time bars then show the answer, and the reveal refers to the learner's pick.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions (compare two poems, 90 minutes for 80 marks, explain a brighter bulb, stuck on a 3-mark question after 6 minutes, evaluate a phone ban) with every wrong option mapped to a specific reason, for example that writing about only one poem is not a comparison, that a preference is not a comparison, and that an equal split ignores the marks.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores Flesch-Kincaid grade 3.6 (learner limit 6.5) and adult text 7.9 (limit 9.5). Each command word is defined in plain words with its signal words (because, so, whereas), and lab cards are one or two short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no filler. Kid paragraphs cover command words, the four meanings, marks and timing, and mark schemes with past papers; the adult text gives the exam board basis, what the lab does, named mistakes and one routine for home.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots before and after Show me at every step. The first version spilled the longest reason chip out of its box and clipped the paper header at 360 px, so the chip text was shortened, chips made taller and the header cut to '45 min paper, 40 marks, 5 min to check'. Every canvas target has a labelled button twin below.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme. The canvas aria-label and live status line read the state (marks so far, minutes per question, which pan each point is in, the mark given to each answer), time bars and pans also work by labelled buttons, and challenge feedback is announced in a polite live region.
